intro: You've been putting it off for years — the avocado-coloured bathroom suite, the cramped shower cubicle, the tray that's cracked along one edge. If you're a homeowner in East Kilbride thinking about a proper wet room installation, you're in good company. Demand has grown steadily across the town as people invest in their homes rather than move, and wet rooms have become the go-to upgrade for anyone who wants a bathroom that's both genuinely practical and genuinely good-looking. Whether you're planning for accessibility, simply want more space, or just want a bathroom that doesn't embarrass you when guests visit, a professionally installed wet room transforms how you use the room every single day.
localContext: East Kilbride is a town with real variety in its housing stock, and that variety matters when it comes to wet room installation. Older Edwardian semis — particularly those in the established streets closer to the town centre — often have suspended timber floors and relatively compact bathroom footprints, which means a wet room requires careful structural assessment and sometimes additional reinforcement before tanking and drainage can begin. Post-war estate properties, which make up a large proportion of East Kilbride's housing, tend to have solid concrete floors in bathrooms, which actually simplifies the drainage installation considerably. Modern developments on the outskirts are usually better suited structurally, though they often come with smaller bathrooms where clever design is essential. East Kilbride sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth knowing because limescale build-up on glass panels and fittings is a real consideration — many local installers will recommend either a water softener or limescale-resistant coatings as part of the project.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in East Kilbride typically follows a clear sequence of work, and understanding each stage helps you plan realistically. The process starts with a full strip-out of the existing bathroom — removing the old suite, tiles, and flooring — followed by a structural inspection to confirm the floor can handle the load and moisture demands of a fully waterproofed space. For timber-floored properties, this often means adding a cement board substrate before anything else happens. The tanking stage is arguably the most critical: a specialist waterproof membrane is applied across the entire floor and up the walls to a minimum height, usually 1.8 metres, to create a completely watertight zone. This is where corners get cut by inexperienced traders and where leaks originate, so it's worth asking your installer specifically about the tanking system they use. Once the membrane is cured and tested, the wet room drain is set into the floor — linear drains along one wall are popular in East Kilbride homes as they suit the proportions of most local bathrooms and make cleaning straightforward. Tiling follows, with the floor laid to a precise gradient toward the drain, then the new suite, shower fixtures, and screen are fitted. A good installer will do a final water test before signing off. From start to finish, most wet room projects in East Kilbride take between five and ten working days depending on the size of the room and the specification of the fittings.
pricing: In East Kilbride, a realistic budget for a full wet room installation sits between £6,000 and £12,000 for most homes. The lower end typically covers a straightforward solid-floor bathroom with a mid-range finish — good quality tiling, a reliable drain, and standard fixtures. The upper end reflects properties with timber floors needing structural work, larger rooms, premium Italian or Porcelain tile selections, thermostatic shower systems, underfloor heating, or bespoke glass screens. Labour costs in South Lanarkshire are broadly similar to the Central Belt average, so the main variables are the condition of your existing bathroom and the specification you choose. It's worth budgeting a small contingency — around ten percent — for older properties where hidden issues sometimes emerge once the strip-out begins.
whyLocal: Hiring a tradesperson who knows East Kilbride well genuinely makes a difference on a project like this. Someone who has worked across the town's mix of Edwardian semis, post-war council-built properties, and modern estate homes understands the quirks you're likely to encounter — whether that's the way older properties were plumbed, the typical floor constructions you'll find in different streets, or the suppliers in the area who can turn materials around quickly. A local installer also has a reputation to protect in a mid-sized town where word travels fast, which tends to focus minds on doing the job properly rather than rushing to the next one.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in a timber-floored bathroom in an East Kilbride Edwardian semi?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires extra preparation. The joists and subfloor need to be assessed for strength, and a cement board or similar rigid substrate must be laid before tanking begins. It adds cost and time — typically an extra day's work and several hundred pounds — but it's entirely achievable and done regularly in East Kilbride's older housing stock.

faqs.q: How do I deal with limescale on my wet room glass in East Kilbride's hard water?
faqs.a: East Kilbride's moderately hard water does mean limescale on glass screens is a genuine nuisance. The most practical solutions are either fitting a whole-house water softener at the same time as your wet room, or specifying glass panels with a hydrophobic coating applied at the factory. Both options are worth discussing with your installer before the project starts rather than retrofitting later.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take from start to finish?
faqs.a: For most East Kilbride homes, plan for five to eight working days — roughly one to two weeks. Smaller rooms in modern developments often come in at the shorter end; larger bathrooms or those needing structural floor work in older properties will take longer. Your installer should give you a clear programme before work starts so you can plan around being without a bathroom.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission or building warrants for a wet room in East Kilbride?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. A wet room replacing an existing bathroom in a standard East Kilbride property is covered under permitted development and doesn't require a building warrant from South Lanarkshire Council. The exception might be if your property is listed or in a conservation area, which is uncommon in East Kilbride but worth confirming. Your installer should be familiar with the local requirements.
